name: The Empty Chair
objective: At least one cell in every grid must still be empty when the show ends.
payoff: The empty cell pays out its grid's row term again as tips.
counterplay: Any card that removes a placed card; the auto-fill blind is its direct enemy.
reference: The one seat kept free for the ghost of the house.

name: Five Couples
objective: At least five pairs must have scored across the whole board.
payoff: Every pair after the fifth scores double.
counterplay: Rank-fixing clowns; Slapstick and Custard Pie both manufacture pairs.
reference: Pinochle's marriages, counted rather than named.

name: The Twenty-Thirty
objective: At least one scored line must have ranks summing to between twenty and thirty inclusive.
payoff: That line scores as though it were one hand better than it is.
counterplay: Face-cards-count-ten changes every sum; rank-shifting cells do it cell by cell.
reference: Cribbage's counting phase, bounded into a window.

name: Family Resemblance
objective: At least one cell coordinate must hold the same rank in every open grid.
payoff: Each matching coordinate pays the special bucket once.
counterplay: Cross-grid movement - Teleport Boxes, Cannon Woman, Walking Through Walls.
reference: The multi-grid objective that only exists because grids align.

name: Nothing Matching
hazard: At least one row must contain no flush and no four of a kind.
payoff: The plainest row on the board scores its rank sum as flat points.
counterplay: Suit-changing clowns can break a flush you accidentally built.
reference: The anti-flush hand the five-suit note asks for.

name: The Descending Act
objective: One column must read in strict ascending or descending rank from top to bottom.
payoff: That column scores as a straight regardless of what it actually is.
counterplay: Selection-sort and Liberty Horses both reorder; Slapstick fixes one mistake.
reference: President's climbing rule as a single-column goal.

name: Sight Unseen
hazard: Every card is face down in the Entrance and only turns face up once placed.
payoff: Every card placed blind that completes a line scores double.
counterplay: Crystal Ball, Madame Zora's Eye and any deck-vision effect see through it.
reference: The owner's own line - some cards show up flipped until placed.

name: The Ranked Floor
hazard: Scattered cells add or subtract from the rank of whatever is placed on them, shown before you commit.
payoff: A card placed on a subtracting cell scores its original rank as bonus tips.
counterplay: Rank-growth cards absorb a penalty; Expanding Dice climbs back out of one.
reference: Mancala cells, made visible. Candy-crush's board modifiers.

name: Dress Code
hazard: Some cells demand a named suit and refuse anything else.
payoff: A card that satisfies a demanding cell scores its suit effect twice.
counterplay: Custard Pie repaints a suit; the Harlequin pip satisfies two demands at once.
reference: The suit-forcing cell, in its restrictive reading.

name: The Dye Vat
hazard: Some cells convert whatever is placed on them to a named suit.
payoff: Converted cards count for both suits when the line scores.
counterplay: Anything that wants a flush; anything that hates one.
reference: The suit-forcing cell, in its generous reading.

name: The Understudy Fills In
hazard: Any grid you place nothing into during a refill has a random card placed in it for you.
payoff: A random placement that completes a line scores triple - the understudy got lucky.
counterplay: Spreading placements across grids; Shy Clown buys a slot back.
reference: Punishes ignoring a grid, which is otherwise the dominant line.

name: The Sealed Envelope
hazard: One card starts face down somewhere in a grid and is only revealed when a card is placed beside it.
payoff: Revealing it scores its rank times the number of cards already adjacent.
counterplay: Deliberately building toward it; any reveal effect.
reference: The crystal-ball act, where the answer was sealed in advance.

name: Lost Ring
hazard: One grid is closed for the whole show.
payoff: Every remaining grid scores double.
counterplay: Deck thinning - fewer cards means fewer grids expected, so less is lost.
reference: The weight-two example the owner names. The doubling is the compensation.

name: Rent Per Cell
hazard: Every cell you use costs a flat amount off the final total.
payoff: Any line completed with fewer than five of your own cards is exempt.
counterplay: Playing small and sharp; the empty-chair objective agrees with this one.
reference: The owner's more granular alternative to losing a whole grid.

name: Knifetown
hazard: Knives melds score nothing.
payoff: Every non-Knives meld scores an extra flat bonus, and Knives cards still pay tips.
counterplay: A rainbow deck; Custard Pie repaints the offending suit.
reference: The town that has seen enough knife throwing.

name: Firetown
hazard: Flames melds score nothing, and Burning cannot be applied.
payoff: Cards that would have burned instead gain a permanent rank.
counterplay: Suit variety; the Fire Marshal's own answer card.
reference: Post-Hartford fire regulation, as a town's mood.

name: Juggletown
hazard: Balls melds score nothing, and Juggling pays out at half.
payoff: Every Juggling status held at show end converts to tips instead.
counterplay: Anything that scores on placement rather than on a later score.
reference: The town that has seen every juggler on the circuit.

name: Hooptown
hazard: Hoops melds score nothing, and hoop props pass through without paying.
payoff: Talent cards a hoop passes gain a charge instead of scoring.
counterplay: Talent-light rows; knives do the opposite work.
reference: The fourth taste, completing the set.

name: Hey Rube
hazard: Each refill, the rightmost column is brawled over - every card in it is debuffed.
payoff: A Stuntsman or Strongman placed in that column defends it and scores for every card it saved.
counterplay: The Escape Artist class exists for exactly this.
reference: The historical rallying cry when a circus fought the locals.

name: Blowdown
hazard: At show start and at every refill, one random Entrance card is discarded.
payoff: Every discarded card returns at show end and scores its rank as tips - the show went on.
counterplay: Entrance mulligan cards; anything that scores from the discard.
reference: Tent blowdowns, the travelling show's most feared weather.

name: Mud Show
hazard: Picking up any card or stack costs one discard.
payoff: Every card that is never picked up after placement scores a flat bonus.
counterplay: Placing well the first time; Rooted and Rosin cards were never moving anyway.
reference: Small circuses slogging unpaved roads between towns.

name: The Fire Marshal
hazard: Flames cards may not be placed at all; they must be discarded from the Entrance.
payoff: Every Flames card discarded this way mints a Gold card.
counterplay: A deck that does not lean on one suit.
reference: Fire regulation that reshaped tenting forever.

name: Temperance Town
hazard: Concessions cards are disabled and shop prices double.
payoff: Every disabled Concessions card scores its rank as flat points at show end.
counterplay: Any class but one; the Grease Joint still filters the deck.
reference: Dry towns on the historical routes.

name: John Robinson
hazard: The show is cut short - the deck is halved before the first draw.
payoff: The fame goal is halved too, and any line completed in the first refill scores double.
counterplay: Fast decks; First Act cards guarantee the opener.
reference: The code phrase that meant cut the show short, tonight.

name: Lot Lice
hazard: The first line scored this show pays nothing - they watched the setup for free.
payoff: Every line after the first scores an extra flat bonus.
counterplay: Deliberately scoring a worthless line first.
reference: Slang for townsfolk who watched the tent go up and never bought a ticket.

name: The Rival Show
hazard: A rival played this town first - the fame goal is raised before you begin.
payoff: Beat it and take one card from the rival's deck into yours.
counterplay: Anything that raises score ceilings; the Hype wager stacks with it.
reference: Barnum against Forepaugh, Ringling against everyone.

name: Railroad Jump
hazard: One card is left on the platform - a random card leaves the deck for this show only.
payoff: The abandoned card returns after the show with a permanent rank increase.
counterplay: Large decks barely notice; small decks feel it exactly.
reference: The brutal overnight railroad jumps of the golden age.

name: The Whip
hazard: Every card triggers one extra time and gains an injury stack for it.
payoff: The extra triggers are real points, and injuries clear if the card sits out the next show.
counterplay: The Net lowers retirement; the Infirmary clears stacks between shows.
reference: Driving performers and animals harder, with the historical cost attached.

name: The Net
hazard: Nothing in this grid can be destroyed, but every line scores less.
payoff: Cards that would have died survive with a permanent rank increase.
counterplay: Decks that were never risking anything lose the least.
reference: Nets turned an audience's fear into awe, and the act was valued less for it.

name: Ringling Modesty
hazard: Only Common and Uncommon cards score - flashy cards pay nothing.
payoff: Every Common card scores triple while the rule holds.
counterplay: A deck that kept its cheap cards; the power-sort chains bottom out here.
reference: The Ringlings sold themselves as the respectable circus.

name: The Water Ring
hazard: The bottom row of every grid is flooded and unusable.
payoff: A card with a diving or aerial feat placed above the flood scores double.
counterplay: Any effect that plays high; the flood only takes the floor.
reference: The ring floor that filled with water for the diving act.

name: Minefield
hazard: Hidden bombs are seeded through every grid; each cell shows how many neighbours are mined, and a card placed on a bomb loses most of its rank.
payoff: Every bomb safely mapped and avoided pays the special bucket.
counterplay: Reading the numbers. It is a solvable puzzle, not a coin flip.
reference: Minesweeper, which the draft names directly.

name: The Mirror Troupe
hazard: The deck doubles with temporary mirror copies of every card; a mirror placed adjacent to its original destroys both.
payoff: Twice the cards to work with, and any mirror that survives to show end scores its original's rank again.
counterplay: Spatial awareness; cross-grid placement keeps pairs apart.
reference: The owner's own boss - resources doubled and a trap laid inside them.

name: Elbow Room
hazard: Every card must be placed adjacent or diagonal to a card already in that grid.
payoff: The grid's first card scores as though it completed a line.
counterplay: Placing the first card centrally; India-Rubber Man ignores placement rules.
reference: Poker Squares' own historical connection rule, used as a restriction.

name: Spread Out
hazard: Each card must go in a column, or a row, that no previously placed card has used, until every one is used.
payoff: Completing the forced spread scores the special bucket once per grid.
counterplay: Cross-grid placement resets the constraint per grid.
reference: The mirror of Elbow Room, from the same owner line.

name: Uno Night
hazard: A card may only be placed adjacent to a card sharing its suit or its rank.
payoff: Any card placed adjacent to a match in both suit and rank scores triple.
counterplay: Wild ranks and the Harlequin pip satisfy anything.
reference: Crazy Eights, as a placement rule.

name: Fan Tan Foundations
hazard: Only sevens may open an empty grid; everything else must build outward by rank within suit.
payoff: Every card placed in sequence off a seven scores an escalating bonus.
counterplay: Any deck holding its sevens; the tutor cards fetch one.
reference: Fan Tan, whose sevens are the only foundations.

name: The Climb
hazard: Each card placed in a column must equal or beat the rank of the one placed before it there.
payoff: A column completed under the climb scores as a straight as well as itself.
counterplay: Low cards first; Slapstick fixes a single blocked column.
reference: President's climbing rule, one column at a time.

name: Forfeit
hazard: Placing a face card forces the next placement to also discard cards - four for an ace, three for a king, two for a queen, one for a jack.
payoff: Every card discarded to a forfeit scores its rank as tips.
counterplay: Number-heavy decks; the discard engine turns the tax into filtering.
reference: Beggar My Neighbor's escalating forfeits.

name: Trump Night
hazard: One suit is named trump; melds without a trump card score at half.
payoff: Melds containing two or more trump cards score double.
counterplay: Any suit-changing effect; the Harlequin pip is always trump.
reference: Whist's trump suit, imported wholesale.

name: Black Maria
hazard: One named suit scores negative when it appears in a meld.
payoff: Negative scores still add to the combo, and the combo applies to everything.
counterplay: The negative-rank family wants exactly this blind.
reference: Hearts, where the queen of spades costs thirteen.

name: The Booking
objective: Declare before the show exactly how many melds you will score, and hit the number exactly.
payoff: Hitting the declaration pays a bonus larger than any meld in the game.
counterplay: Careful, deliberate play. Over-scoring loses as surely as under-scoring.
reference: Oh Hell's bid, which the owner's own note asked to import.

name: Ninety-Nine
objective: Discard three cards before the show; their suits set the number of lines you must score.
payoff: The bid costs you the cards that made it, and hitting it doubles the show.
counterplay: Choosing a low bid you can guarantee.
reference: Ninety-Nine's elegant bidding by discard.

name: Sudoku Ring
objective: No rank may repeat in any row or column of one named grid.
payoff: That grid scores its whole board again as a bonus.
counterplay: Rank-changing clowns; the Blank rank never repeats anything.
reference: The draft's sudoku bonus, promoted to a boss objective.

name: Four Triplets and a Pair
objective: One grid's rows, or its columns, must contain four triplets and a pair between them.
payoff: The completed hand pays the special bucket several times over.
counterplay: Rank duplication effects; Tintype and the copy family.
reference: A mahjong hand read across a whole grid.

name: The Twenty-One
objective: At least one scored line's ranks must total exactly twenty-one, and no line may exceed it.
payoff: The twenty-one line scores as a straight flush.
counterplay: Face-cards-count-ten; the extreme-rank family makes the arithmetic strange.
reference: Blackjack, including the bust.

name: Two Hundred
objective: The board must reach the traditional Barry-scoring total of two hundred before the fame goal counts at all.
payoff: Passing two hundred converts every point above it directly into tips.
counterplay: The historical benchmark is reachable with a clean grid and no effects at all.
reference: Poker Patience's own historical win condition.

name: Leave No Trace
objective: The board must be empty when the show ends.
payoff: Every card removed to satisfy it scores its rank twice.
counterplay: The destruction family finally has a level that wants it.
reference: Burning Man's principle, from the reference compendium.

name: The Peaceful Menagerie
objective: No card may be destroyed or removed for the whole show.
payoff: Every Animal card scores double at the end.
counterplay: Avoiding the destruction family entirely, which most decks can.
reference: The peaceful-animal act, where nothing growls and nothing is subdued.

name: Hall of Mirrors
hazard: Every effect that targets a cell also targets the mirrored cell in the next grid.
payoff: A single effect can now score twice; the trap is that destruction mirrors too.
counterplay: Grid-local effects on the outermost grid have nothing to mirror into.
reference: The midway's mirror maze, and a boss that only multi-grid play can produce.

name: The Marathon
hazard: The show does not end until the deck is empty; End is disabled.
payoff: Every refill after the fifth raises the multiplier permanently.
counterplay: Small decks finish quickly; Cheat Day rewards the cards left over.
reference: Dance marathons and endurance shows, where the act was not stopping.

name: Exposition City
hazard: Only one card of each class may score per refill.
payoff: The first card of each class to score does so at double value.
counterplay: A rainbow deck sails through; a mono-class deck stalls.
reference: A world's fair, where every exhibit gets one turn.

name: The Jaded City
hazard: A meld type that has already scored this show pays half as much every time it repeats.
payoff: The first instance of each meld type scores triple.
counterplay: Meld variety; the secret-meld family is the way out.
reference: A city that has seen the act before, twice.

name: The Gong
hazard: Score too little in any single refill and the show ends immediately.
payoff: Every refill that clears the bar raises the bar and the payout together.
counterplay: Front-loading the board; the Booking pairs badly, on purpose.
reference: The Gong Show's hook, and vaudeville's own.

name: The Loggione
hazard: Common cards score nothing - the gallery are experts and they are not impressed.
payoff: Every Rare or better card scores double.
counterplay: The inverse of Ringling Modesty; one deck answers both badly.
reference: La Scala's gallery, feared by every singer who played it.

name: The Prepared Town
hazard: Every Gaff, Humbug and disguised card is revealed and disabled.
payoff: Each disabled fake mints a Gold card, so the deception still pays.
counterplay: Decks that never leaned on hidden information.
reference: A town that read the newspapers before the show arrived.

name: The Balance
objective: The row term and the column term must end within one point of each other.
payoff: Matching them exactly multiplies the grid's whole score.
counterplay: Deliberate under-scoring, which no other level ever asks for.
reference: Barong against Rangda, where the point is equilibrium, not victory.

name: The Faro Bank
hazard: The house calls one rank before the show; every card of that rank in your deck is dealt against you and scores for the house.
payoff: Beat the house's total and take the whole bank as tips.
counterplay: Thinning that rank out; the Fortune Teller class sees it coming.
reference: Faro, the gambling hall's staple and its most rigged game.

name: The Ban
hazard: One card type or class is outlawed and may not be played at all.
payoff: Every card of the banned kind still in your deck at show end scores its rank as tips - you smuggled it home.
counterplay: The ban-workaround family in the references is built for this.
reference: Oppression into invention - the most repeated story in world performance.

name: The Claque
hazard: The front rows are paid to applaud - the first meld each refill scores double whether it deserved it or not.
payoff: There is no downside this level; it is a good night, and the goal is raised to match.
counterplay: None needed. Not every blind must bite.
reference: The claque, professional applauders sold by the row.

name: Sponsorship
hazard: Gain a Gold card every refill, and lose a flat amount of fame for each one you keep.
payoff: Spend them all before the show ends and the fame comes back doubled.
counterplay: Spending is easy; hoarding is the trap.
reference: The fame tax for taking the money, from the references.

name: The Shredder
hazard: One random card in your deck will destroy itself at show end.
payoff: It pays double for every line it scored before it went.
counterplay: Playing it early and often, which is the point.
reference: The artwork that shredded itself at auction and doubled in value.

name: Day and Date
hazard: A rival plays the same town on the same night - every refill, one of your Entrance cards is bought out from under you.
payoff: Any line completed with a card the rival wanted scores triple.
counterplay: Placing fast; the rival only takes what is still in the Entrance.
reference: Day-and-date booking, the circus wars' dirtiest tactic.

name: The Riot
hazard: Two factions in the crowd fight - at each refill, one row is chosen and its cards are shuffled among themselves.
payoff: A row that still scores after being shuffled pays the special bucket.
counterplay: Flushes and four-of-a-kinds survive shuffling; straights do not.
reference: Rival claques rioting, which is real opera history.

name: The Scam Booking
hazard: The advertised venue does not exist - the grid you commit to first is removed after the first refill and its cards are discarded.
payoff: Every discarded card returns to the deck upgraded.
counterplay: Commit first to the grid you care least about.
reference: A festival that sold tickets to an island with nothing on it.

name: Nuzlocke
hazard: Every card added to the deck after the run began is locked in and can never be traded, sold or removed.
payoff: Locked cards score an escalating bonus for every show they survive.
counterplay: Taking fewer, better cards. It is a whole-run challenge, not one level.
reference: The owner's named challenge layer, sitting above the blinds.

name: The Hype
objective: Double the fame this show demands before it begins.
payoff: Clearing a hyped show doubles the rewards and the odds of rarer cards.
counterplay: Declining. The Hype is always opt-in, which is what makes it fair.
reference: The owner's hype mechanic, kept as a player-chosen blind.

name: The Patient Crowd
hazard: The audience has limited patience - moving a card spends it, and at zero the show ends.
payoff: Every distinct effect triggered refunds patience, so a varied board plays longer.
counterplay: Clown cards raise the ceiling; a full clown set can move for free.
reference: The owner's patience system, deployed as a level rather than a default.

name: Injury Night
hazard: Every trigger risks an injury stack, and enough stacks retire a card for the rest of the run.
payoff: Every injury taken adds permanently to that card's rank if it survives the show.
counterplay: The Net, the Balance Pole and Lloyd's Policy all answer it.
reference: The no-net era, when injuries were constant and the show went on anyway.

name: The Hall of Prodigies
hazard: Only cards with unusual ranks - blanks, wilds, half-steps, negatives - may score.
payoff: Each of them scores triple while the rule holds.
counterplay: The Freakshow class exists for this one level.
reference: The sideshow bill, where ordinary was the one thing that did not sell.

name: Weather Front
hazard: Rain stops the show - nothing scores until a card is placed that covers the ring.
payoff: Once covered, every line scored in the rain pays double.
counterplay: One canvas card in the deck ends the hazard immediately.
reference: Wet weather made performance impossible until canvas covers arrived.

name: The Long Row
objective: One row must be completed continuously across every open grid.
payoff: The long row scores as a straight flush regardless of its contents.
counterplay: Cross-grid movement; Linking Rings makes one suit continuous for free.
reference: The long-row rule, promoted from a permission to a demand.

name: The Tall Order
objective: At least one cell must hold a stack five cards high.
payoff: The stack scores its height line and the whole column again.
counterplay: The height family; Strongman and Iron Jaw hold a tall stack up.
reference: The fourth coordinate, made mandatory for one night.

name: Both Diagonals
objective: Both long diagonals of one grid must score.
payoff: Each diagonal pays the special bucket twice.
counterplay: Spiderweb and the formation family read diagonals natively.
reference: The optional diagonal variation, made compulsory.

name: The Robbers
hazard: Between refills, robbers take the highest-value card off the board.
payoff: A card deliberately left as bait scores triple if it is the one stolen.
counterplay: Spreading value; the theft always takes the single best card, which you choose.
reference: The circus drew merchants and pickpockets alike.

name: Lightning Strike
hazard: Lightning strikes the highest-value card on the board each refill, shocking it and its neighbours.
payoff: A shocked card that still scores pays double - it performed through it.
counterplay: Keeping several cards of similar value so the strike is never decisive.
reference: Electric light and open weather were the same evening.

name: Hurricane
hazard: A storm of a random category from one to five soaks a ring of cells and moves each refill, weakening as it goes.
payoff: Every soaked card that still scores pays out the storm's remaining category as tips.
counterplay: The track is visible a refill ahead, so it can be outrun.
reference: The touring show's oldest enemy, scaled.

name: Tsunami
hazard: A wave rises from the bottom row, capping how tall stacks may be, then recedes.
payoff: Stacks built back up after the wave score their height line twice.
counterplay: Build wide during the wave and tall after it.
reference: The only hazard that attacks the fourth coordinate.

name: FEMA Relief
objective: Survive enough weather levels this run and relief arrives.
payoff: The fame goal drops permanently for the rest of the tour.
counterplay: None needed - it is the reward for having endured the weather blinds.
reference: Disaster relief, arriving several levels too late.

name: Earthquake
hazard: Every placed card is scrambled to a different cell within its own grid at each refill.
payoff: Any line that still scores after a scramble pays the special bucket.
counterplay: Flushes and four-of-a-kinds survive scrambling; straights do not.
reference: The board itself refusing to hold still.

name: Tornado
hazard: A tornado of random scale lifts a square of cards and sets them down elsewhere.
payoff: Cards that land in a completed line score triple.
counterplay: Small tornadoes are survivable; the scale is rolled and shown before it touches down.
reference: Scaled damage from one blind, which keeps it usable at every tier.

name: Eruption
hazard: Burning spreads outward from one cell in an expanding path, and nothing stops it.
payoff: Every Burning card that scores before the fire reaches the edge pays double.
counterplay: There is no counter - the answer is to score fast, which is the point.
reference: The draft's own note - there is no counter to volcanic eruptions.

name: Monopoly
hazard: Scoring a flush of a rank removes that rank from generation for the rest of the run.
payoff: Each removed rank permanently raises the value of the ranks that remain.
counterplay: Your best line becomes unavailable by using it, so spread your scoring.
reference: Winning your way out of your own strategy.

name: Wildfire
hazard: Fire spreads through flammable cards and stops at cards of a named blocking type.
payoff: A firebreak you built yourself scores its whole line again.
counterplay: Terrain - the player lays the blocking cards themselves.
reference: Fire that respects the board you built.

name: Windy Day
hazard: Cards shift one row or column at random each refill because it is too windy to hold them.
payoff: Any line completed despite a shift pays a flat bonus.
counterplay: Small and constant, so exact formations simply cost more.
reference: You dropped your cards; the show goes on.

name: The Boss
hazard: A boss breathes fire on your score each refill, reducing the total you have already banked.
objective: Defeat it with named hands, or with raw points.
payoff: Beating it with the named hands instead of raw points doubles the reward.
counterplay: Scoring faster than it burns, or hitting the named hands early.
reference: A score that can go down, which changes the pacing of a whole show.

name: The Swarm
hazard: Cards are eaten from the edge of the board inward over several refills.
payoff: Every eaten cell reclaimed by placing over it scores double.
counterplay: Playing outward instead of inward, which fights every other instinct.
reference: Attacks the edges, where the diagonals and long rows live.

name: The Impostor
hazard: One card in the deck is a fake - it costs you score when played, and on some refills it ignores the rules entirely.
objective: Find it and remove it.
payoff: Removing the impostor refunds every point it cost, doubled.
counterplay: Deduction. Its rule-breaking is the clue that gives it away.
reference: The best pure-deduction hazard in the notes.

name: Deja Vu
objective: Every card must be placed in a cell that was occupied at some point earlier this show.
payoff: Each reoccupied cell scores its previous occupant's rank again.
counterplay: Removal effects create the cells this objective needs.
reference: A board that remembers what stood where.

name: Pot of Greed
hazard: Cards left alone in a row are discarded at the next refill.
payoff: Each discarded loner draws two replacements.
counterplay: Placing in pairs, or embracing it as a draw engine.
reference: Isolation punished and rewarded in the same clause.
